did_you_know.text: Did you know? After the Passover festival ended, the Israelites broke up the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and demolished the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh. Then each person returned to his own inheritance and city.

Did you know? Hezekiah reorganized the divisions of the priests and Levites so that each one would serve according to his assigned duty in the offerings, the fellowship offerings, the thanksgiving offerings, and the praise at the gates of the camps of the LORD.

Did you know? Hezekiah set aside from his personal possessions his share for the public sacrifices: the morning and evening burnt offerings, as well as the sacrifices for Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed festivals, as written in the Law of the LORD.
Did you know? Hezekiah commanded the inhabitants of Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their allotted portions, so that they could devote themselves fully to the Law of the LORD.

Did you know? When the command was issued, the Israelites brought abundant offerings of the firstfruits of grain, new wine, olive oil, honey, and all the produce of the fields, as well as tithes of everything.
Did you know? The heaps of offerings began to be piled up in the third month and were completed in the seventh month, meaning that the collection continued for several months.

Did you know? Azariah the chief priest, from the house of Zadok, explained that the people had already brought more than enough: the priests had eaten and were satisfied, and a great surplus still remained because the LORD had blessed His people.

Did you know? The offerings, tithes, and dedicated gifts were brought faithfully, and Hezekiah appointed the Levite Conaniah as supervisor, with his brother Shimei as deputy, along with additional officials to manage the distribution.

Did you know? The chapter also describes an organized register of those serving in the sanctuary: the priests were recorded according to their ancestral families, and the Levites aged twenty and older were recorded according to their divisions and duties.

Did you know? The chapter’s conclusion presents Hezekiah as one who did what was good, right, and true before the LORD, acting wholeheartedly in matters concerning the house of God, the Law, and the commandments.
